summary: Unite the two I Infectum sections, preserving every example and ID.
rationale: Both have the same stem, form and voice; their counts must be combined before selecting examples.

summary: Restore the corpus pronoun suffix: aʕlix → aʕlux
rationale: The supplied 52/39 reads “d mitaʕiqo aʕlux w məsnoqatli”. The entry changes the consonant-bearing pronoun suffix to the feminine -ix, although the same addressee has masculine -ux in qalinayḏux and l-gabux. Restore the corpus reading.

summary: New box Preterit-wa: example for sense 3 in Preterit-wa (Jan 1.33/1408)

data.turoyo: I naqqa d ʕayqowa ʕal Məḏyaḏ, fətḥiwonne lu ʕamo. U ʕamo nuqalwo w šutanwo mənayye. W d ʕayqowa aʕlayye nəqliwo bag gawde, bat tanagayat ʕal aḥ ḥmore mə Karǧos, mə Kafro, mə ‘Kahniya Kur‘ əmmiwola. Manṭanwo maye, hawxa.
data.translation: When things became difficult for Midyat, they would open them for the people. The people would draw water and drink from them. And when things became difficult for them, they would carry it in waterskins, in tin cans on donkeys, from Karjos, from Kafro, from what they called ‘Kahniya Kur’. They would bring water, like that.

rationale: Thin round-1 box; repeated situational ʕal-affected frame with town and plural people.

summary: New box Preterit-wa: example for sense 1 in Preterit-wa (Jan 2.4/569)

data.turoyo: Huwe aṯi l rišayna. Be aydarbo aq qatəl du babo wayna aḥna. ʕAqwole bu šəklano mənayna.
data.translation: He came to be over us. Well, it was as though we were his father's killers. He was annoyed by us like this.

rationale: First I.1 Preterit-wa cell; contracted ʕaq- with experiencer -le and m-stimulus.

summary: Impersonal I.1 retains 3sg.m predicate shape with l-experiencer, including independent hiye or ono; m- marks stimulus. Avoid calling the l-suffix an agent in these emotional predicates.
The inherited ruḥo plus ʕal pattern (I.2, LB154) remains numbered separately. Bare feminine adversity at 99/84 is grouped with I.3, without reconstructing a ruḥo noun.
III pressure targets take ʕal, while heart can be subject in its Detransitive. Existing III examples at 52/39,69/61,75/12,76/20 and84/7 are not new attestations.
New -wa boxes distinguish earlier constricted breathing (Preterit-wa) from continuing aversion (Infectum-wa). Supplied German has no authority to insert a Turoyo can-verb or negation.

Round-1 I.1b aversion and I.3 widening are retained as baseline, not re-proposed. Jan annoyance does not independently establish aversion. I.1 Preterit Intransitive and combined Infectum already have adequate cumulative examples.
The two inherited I Infectum sections are counted together, following round 1. Their unassigned introductory bundle is not used to manufacture a new sense.

maʕiqi after d lə at 1.42/1844 is semantically affected-party distress but bare morphology does not securely identify Detransitive Preterit versus a reduced Infectum. maʕəqlan at 2.1/8 and maʕəqwoli at 2.13/3335 do not resolve L-agent versus affected-experiencer structure from English alone. No speculative new III Preterit-wa box is added.
The explicit plural maʕiqe + past copula documents a Detransitive state. It does not imply an expressed external agent or by itself demonstrate political persecution.
Does kʕuyaqqe have default singular experiencer for a collective, or contracted plural?
Does breath tightness at MAC NE Mor Barsaumo/4 express boredom, oppression or breathing difficulty? Confirm b hn spacing at115/131.
Does aversion merit 1b, or should the editors further widen sense1? It is supported by contextual contrasts, not the free rendering alone.
What does -la resume in III gmaʕəqla with smoke as masculine subject at76/20?
Confirm feminine ʕayqowa at 1.33/1408 and contracted ʕAqwole at 2.4/569 as Preterit-wa; the former has ʕal-affected parties, the latter l-experiencer and m-stimulus.
Is maʕiqi in 1.42/1844 a Detransitive Preterit, reduced Infectum or another state form, and are the visitors or their hearts the subject?
Resolve -lan of maʕəqlan and -wo-li of maʕəqwoli before assigning agent/experiencer and tense boxes. The English intransitive distress is insufficient.
Does maʕiqe at 2.10/2264–2269 mean social restriction, oppressive pressure or subjective distress? Sarbast and the office-holding discussion favour social freedom as the relevant contrast.
Breath as possessed subject, compared with l-suffixed impersonal distress and ruḥo plus ʕal experiencer.
Pursuer applying physical pressure shares the existing ʕal-target frame; no extra pursuit sense.
Water shortage affecting Midyat and its people confirms round-1 situational tightness with ʕal. It is not a fresh hardship sense or a new Preterit-wa box.
Plural community pressure states contrast with sarbast free; social participants broaden inherited bodily/emotional Detransitive uses without a separate oppression sense.
Experiencer l-suffixes persist across negated tolerance and past annoyance. Most stimuli use m-, but Jonah ʕayəqlox aʕle has ʕal-stimulus, distinct from the ʕal-experiencer of I.3.
